<h1 align="center">
  Vue 3 Select Component
</h1>

<p align="center">
  Accessible select for Vue 3. Type-safe, customizable, with a batteries-included <code>Select</code> or headless primitives.

## What is Vue 3 Select Component?

Headless select built on two APIs that share the same state machine, accessibility behavior, and TypeScript types:

| API | Import | Best for |
|-----|--------|----------|
| **Assembled `Select`** | `vue3-select-component` | Drop-in select with search, clear, multi-select, and sensible defaults |
| **Primitives** | `vue3-select-component/primitives` | Custom UX such as infinite scroll, virtualized lists, or non-standard layouts |

The assembled `Select` is a fixed composition of primitives. It is not a separate implementation.

When defaults are not enough, compose primitives directly or mix both approaches.

## Features

- **Two-way binding** with `v-model` for single and multi-select
- **End-to-end types** that tie `option.value` to `v-model`
- **Search and filter** with custom `filterBy` logic (search is on by default on assembled `Select`)
- **Clear, loading, and disabled states** with familiar boolean props
- **Option groups** via `SelectGroup`, `SelectGroupLabel`, and `SelectSeparator` primitives
- **Create new options** with `createItem` on assembled `Select` or `SelectRoot`
- **Accessible by default** following the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern
- **Teleport the menu** to `document.body` by default (Reka UI Popover under the hood)
- **Style your way** with optional `--vs-*` CSS variables, or fully unstyled primitives with `data-*` hooks
- **Light bundle** with Vue 3.5+ and [Reka UI](https://reka-ui.com/) as the only runtime dependency

## Requirements

- [Vue.js](https://vuejs.org) **3.5+**

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add vue3-select-component
```

```bash
npm install vue3-select-component
```

## Quick start

Import the assembled component and its default styles:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import Select from "vue3-select-component";
import "vue3-select-component/styles";

const selected = ref<string | null>(null);
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selected"
    :options="[
      { label: 'A Wizard of Earthsea', value: 'wizard_earthsea' },
      { label: 'Harry Potter and the Philosopher\'s Stone', value: 'harry_potter', disabled: true },
      { label: 'The Lord of the Rings', value: 'the_lord_of_the_rings' },
    ]"
    placeholder="Select a book"
  />
</template>
```

Styles are opt-in and imported manually (CSP-friendly). You can also import `vue3-select-component/styles.css` directly.

### Multi-select, clear, and search

```vue
<Select
  v-model="selectedTags"
  multiple
  clearable
  :options="options"
  placeholder="Search and select"
/>
```

| Mode | `v-model` type | Default |
|------|----------------|---------|
| Single | `string \| number \| null` | `null` |
| Multi | `(string \| number)[]` | `[]` |

Disable search with `:searchable="false"` when you want a button-only select.

## Import paths

| Import | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `vue3-select-component` | Assembled `Select` (default export) |
| `vue3-select-component/primitives` | Headless primitive components |
| `vue3-select-component/styles` | Default assembled styles (`--vs-*` variables) |
| `vue3-select-component/styles.css` | Same stylesheet (explicit `.css` subpath) |

## Primitives

Compose custom selects from low-level building blocks:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import {
  SelectInput,
  SelectListbox,
  SelectNoOptions,
  SelectOption,
  SelectPopover,
  SelectRoot,
  SelectTrailingIcon,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives";
import "vue3-select-component/styles";

const model = ref<string | null>(null);

const options = [
  { value: "js", label: "JavaScript" },
  { value: "ts", label: "TypeScript" },
];
</script>

<template>
  <SelectRoot
    v-model="model"
    :options="options"
    searchable
  >
    <SelectTrigger>
      <SelectValue placeholder="Pick a language" />
      <SelectInput />
      <SelectTrailingIcon />
    </SelectTrigger>

    <SelectPopover>
      <SelectListbox>
        <SelectNoOptions>No results</SelectNoOptions>
        <SelectOption
          v-for="opt in options"
          :key="opt.value"
          :value="opt.value"
          :label="opt.label"
        />
      </SelectListbox>
    </SelectPopover>
  </SelectRoot>
</template>
```

Available primitives include `SelectRoot`, `SelectTrigger`, `SelectValue`, `SelectInput`, `SelectIcon`, `SelectTrailingIcon`, `SelectClear`, `SelectPopover`, `SelectListbox`, `SelectOption`, `SelectGroup`, `SelectGroupLabel`, `SelectSeparator`, `SelectTag`, `SelectNoOptions`, and `SelectCreateItem`.

Advanced patterns such as virtualized lists, infinite scroll, and remote data fetching are documented as primitives recipes, not assembled `Select` APIs. See the [complex use cases guide](https://vue3-select-component.vercel.app/guide/complex-use-cases).

## TypeScript

Option values and `v-model` stay in sync through generics:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component";
import { ref } from "vue";
import Select from "vue3-select-component";
import "vue3-select-component/styles";

type UserOption = SelectOptionData<number> & { username: string };

const selectedUser = ref<number | null>(null);

const userOptions: UserOption[] = [
  { label: "Alice", value: 1, username: "alice15" },
  { label: "Bob", value: 2, username: "bob01" },
];
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selectedUser"
    :options="userOptions"
    :get-option-label="(option) => `${option.label} (${option.username})`"
    placeholder="Pick a user"
  />
</template>
```

See the [TypeScript guide](https://vue3-select-component.vercel.app/guide/typescript) for model types, custom option shapes, and primitive generics.

## Styling

Import `vue3-select-component/styles` for the assembled `Select`, then customize with `--vs-*` CSS variables. Primitives ship unstyled and expose stable `data-*` hooks for your design system.

See the [styling guide](https://vue3-select-component.vercel.app/guide/styling).

## Nuxt

Works in Nuxt 3 and 4 with no dedicated module. Import the stylesheet once in `nuxt.config.ts`:

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  css: ["vue3-select-component/styles"],
});
```

See the [Nuxt guide](https://vue3-select-component.vercel.app/guide/nuxt) for SSR, SSG, and hydration notes.

## Migrating from v0

Still on v0? See the [v0 documentation](https://v0-vue3-select-component.vercel.app/).

See the full [migration guide](https://vue3-select-component.vercel.app/guide/migration) from v0 to v1.

## Contributing & development

This repository is a pnpm workspace:

| Package | Path | Purpose |
|---------|------|---------|
| `vue3-select-component` | `src/` | Published library |
| `@vue3-select-component/playground` | `playground/` | Interactive demos |
| `@vue3-select-component/docs` | `docs/` | Documentation site ([vue3-select-component.vercel.app](https://vue3-select-component.vercel.app/)) |

### Getting started

1. Clone the repository and check out `v1-dev`
2. Install dependencies: `pnpm install`
3. Start local development: `pnpm run dev`

`pnpm run dev` watch-builds the library and runs the playground. The playground resolves library source from `src/` for fast feedback during component work.

### Workspace scripts

| Script | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `pnpm run dev` | Watch-build lib + styles, run playground |
| `pnpm run dev:lib` | Watch-build lib + styles only |
| `pnpm run dev:playground` | Playground dev server only |
| `pnpm run dev:docs` | Documentation dev server |
| `pnpm run docs:dev` | Watch-build lib + docs dev server |
| `pnpm run docs:build` | Build lib + generate static docs |
| `pnpm run build` | Build all workspace packages |
| `pnpm run test` | Run library tests with coverage |
| `pnpm run lint` | Lint the monorepo |

### Library build output

| Output | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `dist/index.es.js` | Assembled `Select` entry |
| `dist/primitives.js` | Headless primitives entry |
| `dist/styles.css` | Minified default styles |

### Contributing guidelines

- **Branching** — `v1-dev` for v1 integration, `master` for releases, `v0` for v0 maintenance
- **Commits** — Conventional commits
- **Tests** — PRs should include tests and pass `pnpm run test` and `pnpm run build`
- **Docs** — Update `docs/` when changing public API or behavior

## Releases

Changelog and release notes are on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/TotomInc/vue3-select-component/releases).

# AGENTS.md

Source: https://github.com/totominc/vue3-select-component/blob/master/AGENTS.md

## Learned User Preferences

- Playground demos should be separate Vue components per test case so manual regression testing stays easy when changing the select.
- Docs use simple, short phrasing (about one to two sentences per section); avoid em-dash and semicolon-heavy prose.
- Interactive docs demos must use `ClientOnly` or `.client` component suffixes to prevent hydration errors.
- Do not add v0-to-v1 migration shims or v0 prop aliases in v1 code; document breaking changes in docs only.
- New primitives API (slots, icons, clear button, empty state, etc.) should be exposed on assembled `Select` where it makes sense.
- When teleport-related unit tests stay flaky after reasonable effort, remove the blocking test and revisit later rather than blocking delivery.
- Prefer correcting default behavior over adding opt-in props when fixing reported UX issues.
- Behavior and composable fixes should cover both primitives and assembled `Select`, with tests.
- ESLint shared config and consumer configs should be TypeScript (`eslint.config.ts`), not JavaScript; use ESLint native TS support with `jiti` on Node.

## Learned Workspace Facts

- v1 is a headless select: low-level building blocks in `src/primitives/` and a batteries-included layer in `src/assembled/Select.vue`.
- The repo is a pnpm workspace with `eslint-config` (shared ESLint), `src` (library), `docs` (Docus/Nuxt), and `playground` (Vite dev server only).
- Shared ESLint config lives in `@vue3-select-component/eslint-config`; packages consume it via local `eslint.config.ts` files (with `jiti`).
- Docs and playground consume the library through workspace package linking to built `dist/`, not fragile source aliases.
- Dropdown positioning uses Reka UI Popover with teleport-to-body as the default for assembled and primitive selects.
- The library is built with Vite, unplugin, and unplugin-dts.
- Docs deploy as static SSG via `nuxt generate`; Vercel output directory is `docs/.vercel/output/static`.
- Complex use cases (virtualized lists, infinite scroll, remote data) are primitives recipes in the guide, not assembled `Select` APIs.
- Assembled `Select` defaults `searchable` to `true`.
- v1 documentation is deployed at `vue3-select-component.vercel.app`; v0 documentation at `v0-vue3-select-component.vercel.app` on the `v0` branch.

---

# 1.introduction.md

Source: https://github.com/totominc/vue3-select-component/blob/master/docs/content/1.getting-started/1.introduction.md

title: Introduction
description: What Vue 3 Select Component is and when to use it
  title: Introduction | Vue 3 Select Component
  description: Learn what Vue 3 Select Component is, when to use the assembled Select versus headless primitives, and how it improves on native HTML selects.
  icon: i-lucide-house

Vue 3 Select Component is an accessible select for Vue 3. It focuses on developer experience, type safety, and ease of use.

## What is Vue 3 Select Component?

v1 has two APIs:

- **Assembled `Select`**: drop-in component with familiar DX from earlier versions.
- **Primitives**: composable building blocks (`SelectRoot`, `SelectTrigger`, `SelectPopover`, and more) for custom UX.

Both APIs share the same state machine, accessibility behavior, and TypeScript types.

## What you can do

- **Bind data with `v-model`**: single or multi-select with two-way binding
- **Search and filter options**: built-in search with custom filter logic
- **Customize rendering**: primitive slots for options, values, tags, icons, and empty states
- **Style your way**: default assembled styles with `--vs-*` variables, or unstyled primitives with `data-*` hooks
- **Teleport the menu**: render the dropdown anywhere in the DOM

## When to use it

Use the **assembled `Select`** for a production-ready select with sensible defaults. Good for migrations from `vue-select` or Vue 2.

Use **primitives** when you need custom UX like infinite scroll, custom positioning, or non-standard layouts.

::note
This documentation covers the v1 API. Still on v0? See the [v0 documentation](https://v0-vue3-select-component.vercel.app/). For upgrade steps, see the [migration guide](/guide/migration).

---

# 2.installation.md

Source: https://github.com/totominc/vue3-select-component/blob/master/docs/content/1.getting-started/2.installation.md

title: Installation
description: Install Vue 3 Select Component in your project
  title: Installation | Vue 3 Select Component
  description: Install vue3-select-component with npm, pnpm, or yarn. Import the Select component or primitives, add styles, and meet the Vue 3.5+ peer dependency.
  icon: i-lucide-download

## Prerequisites

[Vue.js](https://vuejs.org) **3.5+** is required.

## Install the package

::code-group
```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add vue3-select-component
```

```bash [npm]
npm install vue3-select-component
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add vue3-select-component
```

```bash [bun]
bun add vue3-select-component
```

## Import paths

v1 exposes two entry points:

| Import | Use case |
|--------|----------|
| `vue3-select-component` | Assembled `Select` component (default export) |
| `vue3-select-component/primitives` | Low-level primitive components |
| `vue3-select-component/styles` | Default assembled Select styles (`--vs-*` variables) |
| `vue3-select-component/styles.css` | Same stylesheet (explicit `.css` subpath) |

```ts
// Batteries-included
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

// Headless composition
import {
  SelectRoot,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
  SelectPopover,
  SelectListbox,
  SelectOption,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives"
```

## Styling

Import default styles for the assembled `Select`, then customize via `--vs-*` CSS variables (see [Styling](/guide/styling)).

Primitives are headless. Use the default stylesheet or write your own CSS targeting `data-*` hooks.

# 3.usage.md

Source: https://github.com/totominc/vue3-select-component/blob/master/docs/content/1.getting-started/3.usage.md

title: Usage
description: Use the assembled Select component for single and multi-select
  title: Usage Guide | Vue 3 Select Component
  description: Use the assembled Select for single and multi-select in Vue 3. Bind v-model, pass options, set placeholders, enable clearable mode, and handle common props.
  icon: i-lucide-play

The assembled `Select` wires up all primitives with sensible defaults. It is the fastest way to get started.

## Use single select

Try the assembled `Select` in single-select mode:

::client-only
:usage-single-select-demo

#fallback
:select-demo-fallback

Import the component and bind `v-model` to your selected value:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const selected = ref<string | null>(null)
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selected"
    :options="[
      { label: 'Option #1', value: 'option_1' },
      { label: 'Option #2', value: 'option_2' },
      { label: 'Option #3', value: 'option_3' },
    ]"
    placeholder="Select an option"
  />
</template>
```

Your IDE provides autocompletion and type checking automatically.

## Use multi-select

Try multi-select with the `multiple` prop:

::client-only
:usage-multi-select-demo

#fallback
:select-demo-fallback

Bind `v-model` to an array:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const selected = ref<string[]>([])
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selected"
    multiple
    :options="[
      { label: 'Option #1', value: 'option_1' },
      { label: 'Option #2', value: 'option_2' },
      { label: 'Option #3', value: 'option_3' },
    ]"
  />
</template>
```

::note
Upgrading from v0? See the [migration guide](/guide/migration). Props, events, and more have changed.

## Disable search or add clear

Search is enabled by default on the assembled `Select`. Disable it with `:searchable="false"` when you want a button-only select. Add `clearable` to show a clear button when a value is selected.

::client-only
:usage-clearable-demo

#fallback
:select-demo-fallback

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const selected = ref<string | null>(null)

const options = [
  { label: "Option #1", value: "option_1" },
  { label: "Option #2", value: "option_2" },
  { label: "Option #3", value: "option_3" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selected"
    :options="options"
    clearable
    placeholder="Search and select"
  />
</template>
```

## Bind data with v-model

The selected value stays reactive via Vue's `v-model`.

| Mode | `v-model` type | Default |
|------|----------------|---------|
| Single | `string \| number \| null` | `null` |
| Multi | `(string \| number)[]` | `[]` |

[Learn more about `v-model`](https://vuejs.org/guide/components/v-model.html).

- [Browse examples](/guide/examples) for clearable, loading, disabled options, and more
- [Read the assembled deep dive](/guide/deep-dive) to see how primitives are wired together
- [Compose with primitives](/guide/primitives) for full control
- [Configure options](/guide/options) with custom shapes and mappers
- [Browse the API reference](/api/props) for all props and events

# 1.primitives.md

Source: https://github.com/totominc/vue3-select-component/blob/master/docs/content/2.guide/1.primitives.md

title: Primitives
description: Compose custom select UIs with low-level primitive components
  title: Headless Primitives | Vue 3 Select Component
  description: Compose custom select UIs with headless primitives like SelectRoot, SelectTrigger, and SelectOption. Share state and build layouts the assembled Select does not cover.
  icon: i-lucide-blocks

Primitives are headless building blocks that share state via `SelectRoot`. Each one handles a single concern like trigger, popover, or listbox.

## Understand the architecture

```
SelectRoot (state + context provider)
├── SelectTrigger
│   ├── SelectIcon
│   ├── SelectValue
│   ├── SelectInput (when searchable)
│   ├── SelectTrailingIcon
│   └── SelectClear
└── SelectPopover
    └── SelectListbox
        ├── SelectNoOptions
        └── SelectOption (×N)
            └── optional: SelectGroup, SelectGroupLabel, SelectSeparator
```

Cross-component state uses provide/inject. Primitives must live inside `SelectRoot`. Group primitives are optional. Use them only when you need labelled sections or separators in the list.

## Build a searchable single select

```vue [CustomSelect.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import {
  SelectRoot,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
  SelectIcon,
  SelectTrailingIcon,
  SelectClear,
  SelectPopover,
  SelectInput,
  SelectListbox,
  SelectOption,
  SelectNoOptions,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const options = [
  { value: "js", label: "JavaScript" },
  { value: "ts", label: "TypeScript" },
]

const model = ref<string | null>(null)
</script>

<template>
  <div data-assembled-select>
    <SelectRoot v-model="model" :options="options" searchable clearable>
      <SelectTrigger>
        <SelectIcon>
          <UIcon name="i-lucide-code" />
        </SelectIcon>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Pick a language" />
        <SelectInput />
        <SelectTrailingIcon />
        <SelectClear />
      </SelectTrigger>

      <SelectPopover>
        <SelectListbox>
          <SelectNoOptions>No results</SelectNoOptions>
          <SelectOption
            v-for="opt in options"
            :key="opt.value"
            :value="opt.value"
            :label="opt.label"
          />
        </SelectListbox>
      </SelectPopover>
    </SelectRoot>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Register options two ways

**Via `options` prop on `SelectRoot`**: pass a normalized array:

```ts
{ label: string; value: string | number; disabled?: boolean }[]
```

**Via declarative `SelectOption` children**: register options on mount. Both sources merge. Declarative options are skipped when their `value` already exists from the prop.

## Group options

::note
You do not need group primitives for a flat list. Render `SelectOption` children directly inside `SelectListbox`, as in the example above.

Reach for `SelectGroup`, `SelectGroupLabel`, and `SelectSeparator` only when options belong in labelled sections or need visual dividers. Groups and separators are not selectable and do not change keyboard navigation.

```vue [CustomSelect.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import {
  SelectGroup,
  SelectGroupLabel,
  SelectInput,
  SelectListbox,
  SelectOption,
  SelectPopover,
  SelectRoot,
  SelectSeparator,
  SelectTrailingIcon,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const model = ref<string | null>(null)
</script>

<template>
  <SelectRoot v-model="model" searchable>
    <SelectTrigger>
      <SelectValue placeholder="Pick a technology" />
      <SelectInput />
      <SelectTrailingIcon />
    </SelectTrigger>

    <SelectPopover>
      <SelectListbox>
        <SelectGroup>
          <SelectGroupLabel>Frontend</SelectGroupLabel>
          <SelectOption value="vue" label="Vue" />
          <SelectOption value="react" label="React" />
        </SelectGroup>

        <SelectSeparator />

        <SelectGroup>
          <SelectGroupLabel>Backend</SelectGroupLabel>
          <SelectOption value="node" label="Node.js" />
          <SelectOption value="rust" label="Rust" />
        </SelectGroup>
      </SelectListbox>
    </SelectPopover>
  </SelectRoot>
</template>
```

Grouped options still register as normal options. When filtering hides every option in a group, the group label is hidden too.

## Teleport the popover

`SelectPopover` teleports to `document.body` by default so the dropdown escapes overflow and stacking-context constraints. Scoped styles from parent components still apply to slot content after teleport.

Disable teleport or target a custom container with the `teleport` prop:

```vue
<!-- default: teleports to document.body -->
<SelectPopover>
  <SelectListbox />
</SelectPopover>

<SelectPopover teleport="#menu-portal">
  <!-- custom portal target -->
</SelectPopover>

<SelectPopover :teleport="false">
  <!-- render inline -->
</SelectPopover>
```

## Popover behavior

`SelectPopover` wraps reka-ui `Popover`. Pass reka-ui popover props to control placement, collision behavior, modality, and portal deferral:

```vue
<SelectPopover
  side="top"
  :side-offset="8"
  align="end"
  :collision-padding="16"
>
  <SelectListbox />
</SelectPopover>
```

The assembled `Select` accepts the same props and forwards them to `SelectPopover`. See [Popover props](/api/props#popover-props) for the full list.

## Customize with slots

Primitives expose slots for rendering. See [Slots](/api/slots) for the full reference.

| Primitive | Slot | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| `SelectValue` | `default` | Custom single/multi value display |
| `SelectOption` | `default` | Custom option content |
| `SelectGroup` | `default` | Group related options |
| `SelectGroupLabel` | `default` | Label a group for assistive tech |
| `SelectTag` | `default`, `remove` | Custom multi-value tags |
| `SelectIcon` | `default` | Leading icon before the value |
| `SelectTrailingIcon` | `default` | Custom trailing icon or loading UI |
| `SelectNoOptions` | `default` | Custom empty state |

## When to use primitives vs assembled Select

| Use assembled `Select` | Use primitives |
|------------------------|----------------|
| Standard dropdown UX | Custom layouts or infinite scroll |
| Quick integration | Non-standard trigger or popover behavior |
| Migrating from v0 | Full control over every DOM node |

See the [components reference](/api/components) for props and behavior of each primitive.

For how assembled `Select` wires these primitives together, see [Assembled Select deep dive](/guide/deep-dive).

---

# 10.complex-use-cases.md

Source: https://github.com/totominc/vue3-select-component/blob/master/docs/content/2.guide/10.complex-use-cases.md

title: Complex use cases
description: Advanced patterns that go beyond the assembled Select defaults
  title: Complex Use Cases | Vue 3 Select Component
  description: Implement virtualized lists, infinite scroll, remote search, and create-item flows with primitives recipes. Patterns that go beyond assembled Select defaults.
  icon: i-lucide-workflow

These recipes combine primitives with external libraries or custom list rendering. They assume you are comfortable composing `SelectRoot` yourself.

## Virtualized list

Register a large option set on `SelectRoot`, then render only visible rows inside `SelectListbox`. Keyboard navigation and search still run against the full list.

This demo registers 50,000 options and mounts roughly a dozen DOM rows at a time with [VueUse `useVirtualList`](https://vueuse.org/core/useVirtualList/).

::client-only
:example-virtualized-primitives-demo

#fallback
:select-demo-fallback

Install [`@vueuse/core`](https://vueuse.org/) alongside the select package:

::code-group
```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add vue3-select-component @vueuse/core
```

```bash [npm]
npm install vue3-select-component @vueuse/core
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add vue3-select-component @vueuse/core
```

```bash [bun]
bun add vue3-select-component @vueuse/core
```

The example splits into two files:

- Parent select that registers every option `VirtualizedSelect.vue`
- Virtual list child that reads `filteredOptions` from context `VirtualizedOptionList.vue`

::code-group

```vue [VirtualizedSelect.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component"

import { ref } from "vue"
import {
  SelectInput,
  SelectListbox,
  SelectPopover,
  SelectRoot,
  SelectTrailingIcon,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

import VirtualizedOptionList from "./VirtualizedOptionList.vue"

const OPTION_COUNT = 50_000

const allOptions: SelectOptionData[] = Array.from(
  { length: OPTION_COUNT },
  (_, index) => {
    const id = index + 1

    return {
      label: `Option ${id.toLocaleString()}`,
      value: String(id),
    }
  },
)

const selected = ref<string | null>(null)
</script>

<template>
  <div data-assembled-select>
    <SelectRoot
      v-model="selected"
      :options="allOptions"
      searchable
    >
      <SelectTrigger>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Pick from 50,000 options" />
        <SelectInput />
        <SelectTrailingIcon />
      </SelectTrigger>

      <SelectPopover :teleport="false">
        <SelectListbox class="virtualized-listbox">
          <VirtualizedOptionList :total-count="OPTION_COUNT" />
        </SelectListbox>
      </SelectPopover>
    </SelectRoot>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
:deep([data-select-listbox].virtualized-listbox) {
  overflow: hidden;
}
</style>
```

```vue [VirtualizedOptionList.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, watch } from "vue"
import { useVirtualList } from "@vueuse/core"
import {
  injectSelectContext,
  SelectNoOptions,
  SelectOption,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives"

const OPTION_ROW_HEIGHT = 40

defineProps<{
  totalCount: number
}>()

const context = injectSelectContext()

const filteredOptions = computed(() => [...context.filteredOptions.value])

const { list, containerProps, wrapperProps, scrollTo } = useVirtualList(
  filteredOptions,
  {
    itemHeight: OPTION_ROW_HEIGHT,
    overscan: 8,
  },
)

watch(
  () => context.activeOptionValue.value,
  (activeValue) => {
    if (activeValue == null) {
      return
    }

    const activeIndex = filteredOptions.value.findIndex(
      (option) => option.value === activeValue,
    )

    if (activeIndex >= 0) {
      scrollTo(activeIndex)
    }
  },
)
</script>

<template>
  <SelectNoOptions />

  <div
    class="virtualized-option-list"
    v-bind="containerProps"
  >
    <div v-bind="wrapperProps">
      <SelectOption
        v-for="item in list"
        :key="String(item.data.value)"
        :value="item.data.value"
        :label="item.data.label"
        :disabled="item.data.disabled"
        class="virtualized-option-list__row"
      />
    </div>
  </div>

  <p class="virtualized-option-list__stats">
    {{ totalCount.toLocaleString() }} options registered.
    {{ list.length }} rows mounted in the DOM.
  </p>
</template>

<style scoped>
.virtualized-option-list {
  height: var(--vs-menu-height, 200px);
  overflow: auto;
}

.virtualized-option-list__row {
  height: 40px;
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

.virtualized-option-list__stats {
  margin: 0.75rem 0 0;
  padding: 0 0.75rem 0.75rem;
  font-size: 0.8125rem;
  color: #71717a;
}
</style>
```

::note
Pass every option to `SelectRoot` through `:options` so filtering and keyboard navigation stay in sync. Set `:teleport="false"` on `SelectPopover` when the virtual list owns scrolling. Keep a fixed row height on each `SelectOption` so `useVirtualList` can measure correctly. Watch `activeOptionValue` and call `scrollTo` so keyboard focus keeps the active row visible.

## Infinite scroll

Load options in pages as the user scrolls the menu. This demo fetches [JSONPlaceholder](https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/guide/) posts with `_start` and `_limit`, then appends each page to `:options`.

::client-only
:example-infinite-scroll-primitives-demo

#fallback
:select-demo-fallback

Install [`@vueuse/core`](https://vueuse.org/) alongside the select package:

::code-group
```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add vue3-select-component @vueuse/core
```

```bash [npm]
npm install vue3-select-component @vueuse/core
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add vue3-select-component @vueuse/core
```

```bash [bun]
bun add vue3-select-component @vueuse/core
```

The parent owns fetch state. A child list component attaches [`useInfiniteScroll`](https://vueuse.org/core/useInfiniteScroll/) to a scroll container inside `SelectListbox`.

::code-group

```vue [InfiniteScrollSelect.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component"

import { computed, ref } from "vue"
import {
  SelectListbox,
  SelectPopover,
  SelectRoot,
  SelectTrailingIcon,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

import InfiniteScrollOptionList from "./InfiniteScrollOptionList.vue"
import { fetchPostsPage, postToSelectOption } from "./jsonplaceholder"

const PAGE_SIZE = 20

const selected = ref<number | null>(null)
const options = ref<SelectOptionData<number>[]>([])
const totalCount = ref(0)
const isLoading = ref(false)
const isLoadingMore = ref(false)

const hasMore = computed(() => options.value.length < totalCount.value)

async function loadPosts(append: boolean) {
  if (append) {
    if (!hasMore.value || isLoadingMore.value) {
      return
    }

    isLoadingMore.value = true
  }
  else {
    isLoading.value = true
  }

  const { posts, total } = await fetchPostsPage({
    start: append ? options.value.length : 0,
    limit: PAGE_SIZE,
  })

  totalCount.value = total
  const nextOptions = posts.map(postToSelectOption)
  options.value = append ? [...options.value, ...nextOptions] : nextOptions
  isLoading.value = false
  isLoadingMore.value = false
}

function onMenuOpened() {
  if (options.value.length === 0) {
    loadPosts(false)
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <div data-assembled-select>
    <SelectRoot
      v-model="selected"
      :options="options"
      :loading="isLoading"
      @menu-opened="onMenuOpened"
    >
      <SelectTrigger>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Pick a post" />
        <SelectTrailingIcon />
      </SelectTrigger>

      <SelectPopover>
        <SelectListbox class="infinite-scroll-listbox">
          <InfiniteScrollOptionList
            :loaded-count="options.length"
            :total-count="totalCount"
            :is-loading-more="isLoadingMore"
            :has-more="hasMore"
            @load-more="loadPosts(true)"
          />
        </SelectListbox>
      </SelectPopover>
    </SelectRoot>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
:deep([data-select-listbox].infinite-scroll-listbox) {
  overflow: hidden;
}
</style>
```

```vue [InfiniteScrollOptionList.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, useTemplateRef } from "vue"
import { useInfiniteScroll } from "@vueuse/core"
import {
  injectSelectContext,
  SelectNoOptions,
  SelectOption,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives"

const props = defineProps<{
  loadedCount: number
  totalCount: number
  isLoadingMore: boolean
  hasMore: boolean
}>()

const emit = defineEmits<{
  loadMore: []
}>()

const context = injectSelectContext<number>()
const scrollContainer = useTemplateRef("scrollContainer")
const filteredOptions = computed(() => [...context.filteredOptions.value])

useInfiniteScroll(
  scrollContainer,
  () => emit("loadMore"),
  {
    distance: 48,
    canLoadMore: () => props.hasMore && !props.isLoadingMore,
  },
)
</script>

<template>
  <SelectNoOptions />

  <div ref="scrollContainer" class="infinite-scroll-option-list">
    <SelectOption
      v-for="option in filteredOptions"
      :key="String(option.value)"
      :value="option.value"
      :label="option.label"
    />

    <p v-if="isLoadingMore" role="status">Loading more…</p>
  </div>

  <p class="infinite-scroll-option-list__stats">
    {{ loadedCount }} of {{ totalCount }} posts loaded.
  </p>
</template>

<style scoped>
.infinite-scroll-option-list {
  height: var(--vs-menu-height, 200px);
  overflow: auto;
}
</style>
```

```ts [jsonplaceholder.ts]
const POSTS_URL = "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts"

export async function fetchPostsPage(params: { start: number; limit: number }) {
  const url = new URL(POSTS_URL)
  url.searchParams.set("_start", String(params.start))
  url.searchParams.set("_limit", String(params.limit))

  const response = await fetch(url)
  const total = Number(response.headers.get("X-Total-Count") ?? 0)
  const posts = await response.json()

  return { posts, total }
}

export function postToSelectOption(post: { id: number; title: string }) {
  return { label: post.title, value: post.id }
}
```

::note
Register every loaded page on `:options` so keyboard navigation stays correct. Set the listbox overflow to `hidden` and scroll inside a child container so `useInfiniteScroll` can attach to a ref you control. Use `:loading` for the first fetch and a footer row for later pages.

## Remote search

Query a remote API when the user types. This demo debounces `@search` and calls JSONPlaceholder with the `title_like` filter param.

::client-only
:example-remote-search-primitives-demo

#fallback
:select-demo-fallback

::code-group

```vue [RemoteSearchSelect.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component"

import { ref } from "vue"
import { useDebounceFn } from "@vueuse/core"
import {
  SelectInput,
  SelectListbox,
  SelectNoOptions,
  SelectOption,
  SelectPopover,
  SelectRoot,
  SelectTrailingIcon,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

import { postToSelectOption, searchPosts } from "./jsonplaceholder"

const selected = ref<number | null>(null)
const options = ref<SelectOptionData<number>[]>([])
const isLoading = ref(false)

let activeRequestId = 0

function passThroughFilter() {
  return true
}

async function fetchRemoteOptions(query: string) {
  const requestId = ++activeRequestId
  isLoading.value = true

  const posts = await searchPosts({ query })

  if (requestId !== activeRequestId) {
    return
  }

  options.value = posts.map(postToSelectOption)
  isLoading.value = false
}

const onSearchDebounced = useDebounceFn(fetchRemoteOptions, 300)

function onMenuOpened() {
  if (options.value.length === 0) {
    fetchRemoteOptions("")
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <div data-assembled-select>
    <SelectRoot
      v-model="selected"
      :options="options"
      searchable
      :loading="isLoading"
      :filter-by="passThroughFilter"
      @search="onSearchDebounced"
      @menu-opened="onMenuOpened"
    >
      <SelectTrigger>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Search posts by title" />
        <SelectInput />
        <SelectTrailingIcon />
      </SelectTrigger>

      <SelectPopover>
        <SelectListbox>
          <SelectNoOptions>
            <template #default="{ searchValue }">
              {{ isLoading ? "Searching…" : `No posts match "${searchValue}"` }}
            </template>
          </SelectNoOptions>

          <SelectOption
            v-for="option in options"
            :key="String(option.value)"
            :value="option.value"
            :label="option.label"
          />
        </SelectListbox>
      </SelectPopover>
    </SelectRoot>
  </div>
</template>
```

```ts [jsonplaceholder.ts]
const POSTS_URL = "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts"

export async function searchPosts(params: { query: string; limit?: number }) {
  const url = new URL(POSTS_URL)

  if (params.query.trim()) {
    url.searchParams.set("title_like", params.query.trim())
  }

  url.searchParams.set("_limit", String(params.limit ?? 50))

  const response = await fetch(url)

  return response.json()
}

export function postToSelectOption(post: { id: number; title: string }) {
  return { label: post.title, value: post.id }
}
```

::note
Set `:filter-by` to pass through server results. Without it, the built-in label filter hides options that do not match the typed string locally. Track a request id or use `AbortController` to ignore stale responses when search changes quickly.

# 11.nuxt.md

Source: https://github.com/totominc/vue3-select-component/blob/master/docs/content/2.guide/11.nuxt.md

title: Nuxt
description: Use Vue 3 Select Component in Nuxt apps with SSR and SSG
  title: Nuxt Integration | Vue 3 Select Component
  description: Use Vue 3 Select Component in Nuxt with SSR and SSG. Avoid hydration mismatches, load styles correctly, and follow client-only patterns for interactive select demos.
  icon: i-simple-icons-nuxt

Vue 3 Select Component works in Nuxt 3 and 4. No dedicated module is required.

## Install

Install the package as usual. See [Installation](/getting-started/installation).

## Import styles

Import the stylesheet once in `nuxt.config.ts`:

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  css: ["vue3-select-component/styles"],
})
```

## Use in pages and components

Bind `v-model` the same way as in a Vite SPA:

```vue [pages/index.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"

const selected = ref<string | null>(null)

const options = [
  { label: "Option #1", value: "option_1" },
  { label: "Option #2", value: "option_2" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selected"
    :options="options"
    placeholder="Select an option"
  />
</template>
```

Primitives work the same way. Import from `vue3-select-component/primitives`.

## SSR and SSG caveats

The select teleports its dropdown to `document.body` by default. That portal is not present during server render and can cause hydration warnings.

Pick one approach:

### `ClientOnly` (recommended)

Wrap the component with [`ClientOnly`](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/api/components/client-only) for the simplest fix.

The control renders on the client only, once hydration is complete. Add a `#fallback` slot if you want to avoid layout shift.

```vue [pages/index.vue]
<template>
  <ClientOnly fallback="Loading...">
    <Select v-model="selected" :options="options" />
  </ClientOnly>
</template>
```

::note
This is what we use to write interactive docs demos in this project.

### Disable teleport

Pass `:teleport="false"` to keep the dropdown in the component tree. The closed trigger hydrates without a portal mismatch. Use this when you need the control in static HTML or inside overflow containers you control.

```vue [pages/index.vue]
<Select
  v-model="selected"
  :options="options"
  :teleport="false"
/>
```

With primitives, set `teleport` on `SelectPopover`.

### Defer portal

Pass `defer` on `Select` or `SelectPopover` to delay teleport until after mount. Keeps default body teleport without wrapping the whole control.

Learn more about [deferred teleports](https://vuejs.org/guide/built-ins/teleport.html#deferred-teleport) and [on Reka-UI popover portal docs](https://reka-ui.com/docs/components/popover#portal).

## Static generation

`nuxt generate` follows the same rules. Use `ClientOnly`, `:teleport="false"`, or `defer` on every page that renders a select. Search and keyboard behavior run after client hydration.

::note
Form attributes (`name`, `id`, `required`, and ARIA props) pass through to the trigger. They work in SSR markup when the control itself is server-rendered.

---

# 2.options.md

Source: https://github.com/totominc/vue3-select-component/blob/master/docs/content/2.guide/2.options.md

title: Options
description: Structure and configure options for Vue 3 Select Component
  title: Options Guide | Vue 3 Select Component
  description: Structure select options with label and value fields, disabled entries, groups, and custom shapes. Learn how the assembled Select normalizes your option data.
  icon: i-lucide-list

The `options` prop populates the dropdown menu.

## Use the basic structure

Each option needs a `label` and a `value`:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const selected = ref<string | null>(null)
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selected"
    :options="[
      { label: 'JavaScript', value: 'js' },
      { label: 'TypeScript', value: 'ts' },
    ]"
    placeholder="Pick a language"
  />
</template>
```

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `label` | Text shown in the dropdown and selected value |
| `value` | Data bound to `v-model` when selected (`string` or `number`) |

::note
Import the `SelectOption` type (exported as `SelectOptionData`) for TypeScript:

```ts
import type { SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component"

const options: SelectOptionData<string>[] = [
  { label: "JavaScript", value: "js" },
]
```

## Disable individual options

Add `disabled: true` to prevent selection:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const selected = ref<string | null>(null)
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selected"
    :options="[
      { label: 'Available', value: 'a1' },
      { label: 'Unavailable', value: 'a2', disabled: true },
    ]"
    placeholder="Pick an option"
  />
</template>
```

Disabled options cannot be selected. They are skipped during keyboard navigation and get `aria-disabled`.

## Use custom option shapes

When your data does not match `{ label, value }`, provide mappers:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

type Country = { id: string; key: string }

const countries: Country[] = [
  { id: "France", key: "fr" },
  { id: "Germany", key: "de" },
]

const selected = ref<string | null>(null)
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selected"
    :options="countries"
    :get-option-label="(o) => o.id"
    :get-option-value="(o) => o.key"
    placeholder="Select a country"
  />
</template>
```

| Prop | Type | Default |
|------|------|---------|
| `getOptionLabel` | `(option) => string` | `option.label` |
| `getOptionValue` | `(option) => string \| number` | `option.value` |

## Customize search filtering

By default, search matches case-insensitive substrings on the option label.

**Assembled `Select`**: filter receives the source option object:

```ts
type GenericFilterByFn<GenericOption> = (
  option: GenericOption,
  label: string,
  search: string,
) => boolean
```

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

type CountryOption = {
  label: string
  value: string
  code: string
}

const selected = ref<string | null>(null)

const options: CountryOption[] = [
  { label: "France", value: "FR", code: "fr" },
  { label: "Germany", value: "DE", code: "de" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selected"
    :options="options"
    :filter-by="(option, label, search) =>
      label.toLowerCase().includes(search.toLowerCase())
      || option.code.toLowerCase().includes(search.toLowerCase())"
    placeholder="Search by name or code"
  />
</template>
```

**Primitives (`SelectRoot`)**: filter receives the registered option:

```ts
type FilterByFn<Value> = (
  option: RegisteredOption<Value>,
  search: string,
) => boolean
```

## Add extended properties

Options can carry extra fields for custom rendering via primitive slots:

```vue [CustomSelect.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import {
  SelectInput,
  SelectListbox,
  SelectNoOptions,
  SelectOption,
  SelectPopover,
  SelectRoot,
  SelectTrailingIcon,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

type LanguageOption = {
  label: string
  value: string
  version: string
  creator: string
}

const selected = ref<string | null>(null)

const options: LanguageOption[] = [
  { label: "JavaScript", value: "js", version: "ES2022", creator: "Brendan Eich" },
  { label: "TypeScript", value: "ts", version: "5.0", creator: "Microsoft" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <div data-assembled-select>
    <SelectRoot v-model="selected" :options="options" searchable>
      <SelectTrigger>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Pick a language" />
        <SelectInput />
        <SelectTrailingIcon />
      </SelectTrigger>

      <SelectPopover>
        <SelectListbox>
          <SelectNoOptions />
          <SelectOption
            v-for="option in options"
            :key="option.value"
            :value="option.value"
            :label="option.label"
          >
            <span>{{ option.label }} ({{ option.version }})</span>
            <span>{{ option.creator }}</span>
          </SelectOption>
        </SelectListbox>
      </SelectPopover>
    </SelectRoot>
  </div>
</template>
```

See [TypeScript](/guide/typescript) for extending option types safely.

---

# 3.multiselect.md

Source: https://github.com/totominc/vue3-select-component/blob/master/docs/content/2.guide/3.multiselect.md

title: Multi-select
description: Enable and work with multiple selections
  title: Multi-Select | Vue 3 Select Component
  description: Enable multi-select mode in Vue 3 Select Component. Manage array v-model values, selected tags, close-on-select behavior, and UX patterns for picking multiple items.
  icon: i-lucide-check-square

Multi-select lets users pick more than one option. Enable it with the `multiple` prop on assembled `Select` or `SelectRoot`.

## Enable multi-select

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const selected = ref<string[]>([])
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selected"
    multiple
    :options="[
      { label: 'JavaScript', value: 'js' },
      { label: 'TypeScript', value: 'ts' },
      { label: 'Vue', value: 'vue' },
    ]"
    placeholder="Select languages"
  />
</template>
```

## Understand model behavior

| Aspect | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| `v-model` type | `(string \| number)[]` |
| Default value | `[]` |
| Selecting | Adds value to the array. Menu stays open. |
| Deselecting | Click a selected option to toggle it off |
| Clear button | Resets to `[]`, emits `optionDeselected(null)` |

## Selected option checkmarks

In multi-select mode, selected options in the dropdown show a checkmark on the right. The assembled `Select` and primitive `SelectOption` render this by default. Override it with the `checkmark` slot on `SelectOption`.

```vue [CustomSelect.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import {
  SelectInput,
  SelectListbox,
  SelectNoOptions,
  SelectOption,
  SelectPopover,
  SelectRoot,
  SelectTrailingIcon,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const selected = ref<string[]>([])

const options = [
  { label: "JavaScript", value: "js" },
  { label: "TypeScript", value: "ts" },
  { label: "Vue", value: "vue" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <div data-assembled-select>
    <SelectRoot v-model="selected" multiple searchable>
      <SelectTrigger>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Pick languages" />
        <SelectInput />
        <SelectTrailingIcon />
      </SelectTrigger>

      <SelectPopover>
        <SelectListbox>
          <SelectNoOptions />
          <SelectOption
            v-for="opt in options"
            :key="opt.value"
            :value="opt.value"
            :label="opt.label"
          >
            <template #checkmark>
              <UIcon name="i-lucide-check" />
            </template>
          </SelectOption>
        </SelectListbox>
      </SelectPopover>
    </SelectRoot>
  </div>
</template>
```

Style the layout with `data-select-option-label` and `data-select-option-checkmark`.

## Hide selected options

By default, selected options stay visible in the dropdown so users can deselect them. Set `hide-selected` on assembled `Select` to remove them from the list:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const selected = ref<string[]>(["js"])

const options = [
  { label: "JavaScript", value: "js" },
  { label: "TypeScript", value: "ts" },
  { label: "Vue", value: "vue" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selected"
    multiple
    hide-selected
    :options="options"
    placeholder="Select languages"
  />
</template>
```

On primitives, pass `hide-selected` to `SelectRoot`:

```vue [CustomSelect.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import {
  SelectInput,
  SelectListbox,
  SelectNoOptions,
  SelectOption,
  SelectPopover,
  SelectRoot,
  SelectTrailingIcon,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const model = ref<string[]>([])

const options = [
  { label: "JavaScript", value: "js" },
  { label: "TypeScript", value: "ts" },
  { label: "Vue", value: "vue" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <div data-assembled-select>
    <SelectRoot v-model="model" multiple hide-selected :options="options" searchable>
      <SelectTrigger>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Select languages" />
        <SelectInput />
        <SelectTrailingIcon />
      </SelectTrigger>

      <SelectPopover>
        <SelectListbox>
          <SelectNoOptions />
          <SelectOption
            v-for="option in options"
            :key="option.value"
            :value="option.value"
            :label="option.label"
          />
        </SelectListbox>
      </SelectPopover>
    </SelectRoot>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Customize tag remove icon

In multi-select mode, each tag shows a remove button. Override the icon on the assembled `Select` with the `tag-remove` slot:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const selected = ref<string[]>(["js"])

const options = [
  { label: "JavaScript", value: "js" },
  { label: "TypeScript", value: "ts" },
  { label: "Vue", value: "vue" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <Select v-model="selected" multiple :options="options">
    <template #tag-remove>
      <UIcon name="i-lucide-x" />
    </template>
  </Select>
</template>
```

The slot receives `{ label, value }` for each tag. On primitives, use the `remove` slot on `SelectTag` or forward it from `SelectValue` with `tag-remove`.

## Display selected values

By default, `SelectValue` renders a `SelectTag` for each selection. Customize tags with primitive slots:

```vue [CustomSelect.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import {
  SelectInput,
  SelectListbox,
  SelectNoOptions,
  SelectOption,
  SelectPopover,
  SelectRoot,
  SelectTag,
  SelectTrailingIcon,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const model = ref<string[]>([])

const options = [
  { label: "JavaScript", value: "js" },
  { label: "TypeScript", value: "ts" },
  { label: "Vue", value: "vue" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <div data-assembled-select>
    <SelectRoot v-model="model" multiple :options="options" searchable>
      <SelectTrigger>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Pick languages">
          <template #default="{ selectedOptions }">
            <SelectTag
              v-for="opt in selectedOptions"
              :key="String(opt.value)"
              :value="opt.value"
              :label="opt.label"
            >
              <template #default="{ label }">
                <strong>{{ label }}</strong>
              </template>
            </SelectTag>
          </template>
        </SelectValue>
        <SelectInput />
        <SelectTrailingIcon />
      </SelectTrigger>

      <SelectPopover>
        <SelectListbox>
          <SelectNoOptions />
          <SelectOption
            v-for="option in options"
            :key="option.value"
            :value="option.value"
            :label="option.label"
          />
        </SelectListbox>
      </SelectPopover>
    </SelectRoot>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Remove values with keyboard

When the menu is open, searchable, and the search field is empty, **Backspace** removes the last selected tag. This updates `v-model` without emitting `optionDeselected`.

## Combine with search and clear

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const selected = ref<string[]>([])

const options = [
  { label: "JavaScript", value: "js" },
  { label: "TypeScript", value: "ts" },
  { label: "Vue", value: "vue" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selected"
    multiple
    clearable
    :options="options"
    placeholder="Search and select languages"
  />
</template>
```

- **Search** filters visible options without affecting selected values
- **Clear** removes all selections at once

# 4.styling.md

Source: https://github.com/totominc/vue3-select-component/blob/master/docs/content/2.guide/4.styling.md

title: Styling
description: Style Vue 3 Select Component with default CSS or data-attribute hooks
  title: Styling Guide | Vue 3 Select Component
  description: Style Vue 3 Select with bundled default CSS or data-attribute hooks. Override trigger, menu, option, and tag appearance without fighting component internals.
  icon: i-lucide-palette

## Default styles for assembled Select

The assembled `Select` ships optional default styles. Import them once in your app entry:

```ts
import "vue3-select-component/styles"
```

Primitives remain **unstyled** unless you import the stylesheet and target their `data-*` hooks yourself.

::note
Styles are not auto-injected (CSP-friendly). Import them manually, as in v0.

## CSS variables

Default styles use `--vs-*` variables (same prefix as v0). They are defined on `:root`, `[data-assembled-select]`, and `[data-select-popover]` so teleported dropdown panels inherit your theme.

Override variables on the assembled select root:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const value = ref<string | null>(null)

const options = [
  { label: "Option #1", value: "option_1" },
  { label: "Option #2", value: "option_2" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <Select v-model="value" :options="options" class="brand-select" />
</template>

<style scoped>
.brand-select {
  --vs-border-radius: 12px;
  --vs-outline-color: #0ea5e9;
}
</style>
```

Because the popover teleports to `document.body`, set popover-specific variables on `:root` or `[data-select-popover]` when needed:

```css
:root {
  --vs-menu-box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.12);
}
```

### Variable reference

```css
:root {
  --vs-width: 100%;
  --vs-min-height: 38px;
  --vs-padding-y: 4px;
  --vs-padding-x: 8px;
  --vs-padding: var(--vs-padding-y) var(--vs-padding-x);
  --vs-border: 1px solid #e4e4e7;
  --vs-border-radius: 4px;
  --vs-font-size: 16px;
  --vs-font-weight: 400;
  --vs-font-family: inherit;
  --vs-text-color: #18181b;
  --vs-line-height: 1.5;
  --vs-placeholder-color: #52525b;
  --vs-background-color: #fff;
  --vs-disabled-background-color: #f4f4f5;
  --vs-outline-width: 1px;
  --vs-outline-color: #3b82f6;

  --vs-menu-offset-top: 8px;
  --vs-menu-height: 200px;
  --vs-menu-border: var(--vs-border);
  --vs-menu-background-color: var(--vs-background-color);
  --vs-menu-box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05);
  --vs-menu-z-index: 50;

  --vs-option-padding: 8px 12px;
  --vs-option-hover-background-color: #f0f0f0;
  --vs-option-focused-background-color: #dbeafe;
  --vs-option-selected-background-color: #93c5fd;

  --vs-multi-value-background-color: #f4f4f5;
  --vs-multi-value-label-font-size: 12px;
  --vs-multi-value-delete-hover-background-color: #ff6467;

  --vs-icon-size: 20px;
  --vs-trailing-icon-size: 20px;
  --vs-spinner-size: 16px;
}
```

See [`src/styles.css`](https://github.com/TotomInc/vue3-select-component/blob/v1-dev/src/styles.css) for the full list.

## Headless styling with data attributes

Every primitive exposes stable `data-*` hooks for custom CSS:

| Attribute | Element | State |
|-----------|---------|-------|
| `data-select-root` | Root wrapper | |
| `data-assembled-select` | Assembled root | |
| `data-select-trigger` | Trigger button | `aria-expanded` |
| `data-select-value` | Value display | `data-empty` |
| `data-select-input` | Search input | |
| `data-select-popover` | Dropdown panel | `aria-hidden` |
| `data-select-listbox` | Listbox container | |
| `data-select-option` | Option row | `data-value`, `data-active` |
| `data-select-tag` | Multi-value tag | |
| `data-select-tag-remove` | Tag remove button | |
| `data-select-clear` | Clear button | |
| `data-select-icon` | Leading icon | |
| `data-select-trailing-icon` | Trailing icon / loader | `data-open`, `data-loading` |
| `data-select-no-options` | Empty state | |
| `data-select-create-item` | Create action | `data-active` |

### Style the trigger

```css
[data-select-trigger] {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.5rem;
  width: 100%;
  min-height: 2.375rem;
  padding: 0.25rem 0.5rem;
  border: 1px solid #e4e4e7;
  border-radius: 0.375rem;
  background: #fff;
  cursor: pointer;
}

[data-select-trigger]:disabled {
  opacity: 0.5;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
```

### Style options

Use `data-active` for keyboard-highlighted options and `aria-selected` for selected state:

```css
[data-select-option] {
  padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem;
  cursor: pointer;
}

[data-select-option][data-active="true"] {
  background: #dbeafe;
}

[data-select-option][aria-selected="true"] {
  background: #93c5fd;
}

[data-select-option][aria-disabled="true"] {
  opacity: 0.5;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
```

### Style the popover

`SelectPopover` teleports to `document.body` by default. Use global CSS or unscoped styles with `[data-select-*]` hooks. Vue preserves scoped attribute selectors on teleported slot content, but parent `overflow` / `z-index` no longer constrain the panel.

```css
[data-select-popover] {
  margin-top: 0.5rem;
  border: 1px solid #e4e4e7;
  border-radius: 0.375rem;
  background: #fff;
  box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05);
  z-index: 50;
}
```

### Style multi-value tags

```css
[data-select-tag] {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.25rem;
  padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem;
  border-radius: 0.25rem;
  background: #f4f4f5;
  font-size: 0.75rem;
}

[data-select-tag-remove] {
  border: none;
  background: transparent;
  cursor: pointer;
  line-height: 1;
}
```

### Style the trailing icon

```css
[data-select-trailing-icon][data-open="true"] {
  transform: rotate(180deg);
}

[data-select-trailing-icon][data-loading="true"]::after {
  content: "";
  display: inline-block;
  width: 1rem;
  height: 1rem;
  border: 2px solid currentColor;
  border-top-color: transparent;
  border-radius: 50%;
  animation: spin 0.6s linear infinite;
}
```

## Scope styles to a wrapper

Wrap your select in a container class to scope overrides:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const value = ref<string | null>(null)

const options = [
  { label: "Option #1", value: "option_1" },
  { label: "Option #2", value: "option_2" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="my-select">
    <Select v-model="value" :options="options" />
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.my-select {
  --vs-border-radius: 12px;
}
</style>
```

For primitives, scope via a parent class or use `:deep()` as needed.

# 5.typescript.md

Source: https://github.com/totominc/vue3-select-component/blob/master/docs/content/2.guide/5.typescript.md

title: TypeScript
description: Type-safe options, v-model, generics, and custom option shapes
  title: TypeScript Guide | Vue 3 Select Component
  description: Get full TypeScript support for options, v-model, generics, and custom option shapes. Type assembled Select and primitive components with inferred and explicit generics.
  icon: i-lucide-braces

Vue 3 Select Component is built with TypeScript. Types flow from your option data through `v-model`, props, events, and slots so you get autocompletion and compile-time checks in both the assembled `Select` and primitive APIs.

## Generic components

`Select` and `SelectRoot` use [Vue 3.3 generic components](https://vuejs.org/api/sfc-script-setup.html#generics). Two type parameters drive inference:

| Parameter | Default | Role |
|-----------|---------|------|
| `OptionValue` | `string` | The type bound to `v-model` (`string` or `number`) |
| `GenericOption` | `SelectOptionData<OptionValue>` | Your source option objects |

```ts
// Assembled Select: OptionValue first, then GenericOption
Select<OptionValue, GenericOption>

// Primitives: OptionValue only
SelectRoot<OptionValue>
```

TypeScript usually infers both parameters from `:options` and `v-model`. Pass them explicitly when wrapping the component or when inference is ambiguous.

## Use the SelectOptionData type

The canonical option shape is exported as `SelectOptionData` (alias of internal `SelectOption`):

```ts
import type { SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component"

type SelectOptionData<Value extends string | number = string> = {
  label: string
  value: Value
  disabled?: boolean
}
```

::note
v0 exported this type as `Option<T>`. In v1, import `SelectOptionData` instead. See the [migration guide](/guide/migration#update-typescript-imports).

## Configure value types

`option.value` and `v-model` share the same type. Use `string` or `number`:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component"
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

type UserOption = SelectOptionData<number>

const selectedUser = ref<number | null>(null)

const userOptions: UserOption[] = [
  { label: "Alice", value: 1 },
  { label: "Bob", value: 2 },
  { label: "Charlie", value: 3 },
  // { label: "David", value: "invalid" } // Type error
]
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selectedUser"
    :options="userOptions"
    placeholder="Pick a user"
  />
</template>
```

## Extend option properties

Add custom fields and keep them typed in mappers, filters, and events:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component"
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

type UserOption = SelectOptionData<number> & { username: string }

const selectedUser = ref<number | null>(null)

const userOptions: UserOption[] = [
  { label: "Alice", value: 1, username: "alice15" },
  { label: "Bob", value: 2, username: "bob01" },
  { label: "Charlie", value: 3, username: "charlie20" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="selectedUser"
    :options="userOptions"
    :get-option-label="(option) => `${option.label} (${option.username})`"
    placeholder="Pick a user"
  />
</template>
```

With primitives, the same `UserOption` type flows into `SelectOption` slot props and `@option-selected` payloads.

## Validate v-model types

The component enforces consistency between `option.value` and `v-model`:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component"
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

type UserOption = SelectOptionData<number>

// Incorrect: should be ref<number | null>(null)
const selectedUser = ref<string | null>(null)

const userOptions: UserOption[] = [
  { label: "Alice", value: 1 },
  { label: "Bob", value: 2 },
]
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Type error: string conflicts with number -->
  <Select
    v-model="selectedUser"
    :options="userOptions"
    placeholder="Pick a user"
  />
</template>
```

## Use SelectModelValue

The internal `v-model` type is `SelectModelValue<Value>`:

```ts
import type { SelectModelValue } from "vue3-select-component"

type SelectModelValue<Value> = Value | Value[] | null
```

In practice, bind a narrower type for each mode:

| Mode | Bind as |
|------|---------|
| Single select | `ref<Value \| null>(null)` |
| Multi-select | `ref<Value[]>([])` |

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component"
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

type UserOption = SelectOptionData<number>

const single = ref<number | null>(null)
const multi = ref<number[]>([])

const userOptions: UserOption[] = [
  { label: "Alice", value: 1 },
  { label: "Bob", value: 2 },
]
</script>

<template>
  <Select v-model="single" :options="userOptions" />
  <Select v-model="multi" :options="userOptions" multiple />
</template>
```

## Type multi-select refs

When wrapping `Select`, pass both generics so events and options stay typed:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component"
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

type UserOption = SelectOptionData<number>

const selectRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof Select<number, UserOption>>>()
const selectedUsers = ref<number[]>([])

const userOptions: UserOption[] = [
  { label: "Alice", value: 1 },
  { label: "Bob", value: 2 },
]
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    ref="selectRef"
    v-model="selectedUsers"
    :options="userOptions"
    multiple
  />
</template>
```

## Custom value mapping

When options do not follow `{ label, value }`, use `getOptionLabel` and `getOptionValue`. TypeScript infers `GenericOption` from your array:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue"
import Select from "vue3-select-component"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

type Role = { id: string; key: string }

const activeRole = ref<string | null>(null)

const roleOptions: Role[] = [
  { id: "Admin", key: "admin" },
  { id: "User", key: "user" },
  { id: "Guest", key: "guest" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    v-model="activeRole"
    :options="roleOptions"
    :get-option-label="(option) => option.id"
    :get-option-value="(option) => option.key"
    placeholder="Pick a role"
  />
</template>
```

::warning
Custom mappers weaken the link between your array type and `SelectOptionData`. Prefer typed source objects and mappers over casting options to `SelectOptionData[]`. See [Options](/guide/options#use-custom-option-shapes) for runtime behavior.

If inference fails, set generics explicitly:

```vue
<Select<string, Role>
  v-model="activeRole"
  :options="roleOptions"
  :get-option-label="(option) => option.id"
  :get-option-value="(option) => option.key"
/>
```

## Typed events and filters

Assembled `Select` events receive your **source** option object, not the normalized `{ label, value }` shape:

```ts
import type { AssembledSelectEmits, SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component"

type UserOption = SelectOptionData<number> & { username: string }

// optionSelected: [option: UserOption]
// optionDeselected: [option: UserOption | null]
type SelectEvents = AssembledSelectEmits<UserOption>
```

`filterBy` on assembled `Select` also receives the source object:

```ts
type UserOption = SelectOptionData<number> & { username: string }

type FilterBy = (
  option: UserOption,
  label: string,
  search: string,
) => boolean

const filterBy: FilterBy = (option, label, search) =>
  label.toLowerCase().includes(search.toLowerCase())
  || option.username.toLowerCase().includes(search.toLowerCase())
```

On primitives, `SelectRoot` emits `OptionValue` (not the full option object). See [Events](/api/events) for both APIs.

## Import component prop types

All public prop, emit, and slot types are exported for wrappers and design systems:

```ts
import type {
  AssembledSelectProps,
  AssembledSelectEmits,
  AssembledSelectSlots,
  SelectModelValue,
  SelectOptionData,
  SelectPopoverProps,
  SelectRootProps,
  SelectRootEmits,
  SelectTagRemoveSlotProps,
  SelectValueSlots,
} from "vue3-select-component"
```

See [Slots](/api/slots#typescript) for the full list of slot and slot prop types.

Example wrapper:

```ts
import type { AssembledSelectProps, SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component"

type AppSelectProps<T extends string | number> =
  AssembledSelectProps<SelectOptionData<T>, T>
```

## Primitives typing

`SelectRoot` accepts normalized `SelectOptionData<Value>[]` and types `v-model` the same way as assembled `Select`:

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { SelectOptionData } from "vue3-select-component"
import { ref } from "vue"
import {
  SelectListbox,
  SelectNoOptions,
  SelectOption,
  SelectPopover,
  SelectRoot,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "vue3-select-component/primitives"
import "vue3-select-component/styles"

const selected = ref<string | null>(null)

const options: SelectOptionData<string>[] = [
  { label: "JavaScript", value: "js" },
  { label: "TypeScript", value: "ts" },
]
</script>

<template>
  <div data-assembled-select>
    <SelectRoot v-model="selected" :options="options">
      <SelectTrigger>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Pick a language" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectPopover>
        <SelectListbox>
          <SelectNoOptions />
          <SelectOption
            v-for="option in options"
            :key="option.value"
            :value="option.value"
            :label="option.label"
          />
        </SelectListbox>
      </SelectPopover>
    </SelectRoot>
  </div>
</template>
```

Popover-related prop types (`SelectPopoverProps`, `SelectPopoverContentProps`, and others) are exported from the package entry point for custom compositions.
